index.title: Understand DecisioWorks through a production problem
index.intro: When orders, resources or operating rules change, plans need to change with them. DecisioWorks provides production decision capabilities you can embed in business applications: connect data, express trade-offs, generate plans and explain what changed.

sections.title: What do you provide, and what do you get?

blocks.text: Your organization supplies business facts and management judgment. DecisioWorks organizes those inputs into a computational process and returns results for planners or business applications. Commercial deployments can use this process in ongoing operations; a focused first scenario establishes shared definitions.

blocks.caption: Inputs and outputs of a production decision
rows: Orders, products, routes, resources, calendars, and the materials or inventory needed by the scenario
Shared objects, mappings and relationship checks
Delivery and load priorities, allowed adjustments and mandatory rules
Objective and rule configuration, including what is enabled
A capability workflow and runtime resources allowed by the license
Solver status, candidate plans, quantities or job sequences
Business review and actual execution deviations
Metrics, detailed results, comparisons and inputs for the next cycle

blocks.text: Data mappings, rule configurations, case records and industry applications become reusable assets for manufacturers and partners. Available source code makes the calling patterns and decision workflow understandable. Use and distribution follow the license terms of the relevant edition.

items: Manufacturers: choose a planning problem that requires frequent adjustment, and read the cases alongside a sample of your data.
Consultants and industrial parks: turn a diagnosis into concrete data preparation, scenario comparison and business review tasks.
Software partners and developers: start with integration responsibilities, then explore the standard interfaces and open reference implementation.

stamping.title: Stamping: from input data to a reviewable plan
stamping.intro: Start by connecting demand, time and material availability under finite capacity. Then compare the plan after changing management preferences. This guide follows a recorded baseline and re-run.
stamping.context: Recorded 2026-08-31 · DecisioWorks v1.4.0 · Commercial Enterprise license · API records, not a live run on this page

blocks.text: What time-phased production plan can be generated from the given demand, capacity and material conditions? After changing load- and waiting-related objectives, did demand coverage, load or shortages change? Planners need to inspect both physical quantities and how the plan is evaluated.

blocks.title: Evidence from an integrated sample
blocks.text: These figures describe a particular dataset and configuration. They are not a promise of customer outcomes. Quantity coverage, delivery performance and equipment utilization require separate checks.

blocks.caption: Input scale in this sample
rows: Demand items, quantities and due dates
A shared time coordinate for demand, capacity and results
One parent workshop and two production lines, not three machines

blocks.text: The capacity.used field represents the occupied or unavailable proportion, from 0 to 1. It is not the utilization calculated by this solve. Establishing that meaning gives everyone the same capacity baseline.

After reading and checking the data, an orchestration recipe assembles objectives and constraints and calls GOCK to generate a plan. Analysis then examines planned quantities, shortages, load and objective details. The re-run uses the same data and retains configuration differences for review.

sections.title: Output: did the business quantities change?

blocks.caption: Baseline and re-run from the same API comparison

blocks.text: The aggregate business quantities stayed the same, while weighted job_bias changed with its weight. That score change alone does not demonstrate a production improvement. Matching aggregates also do not prove that every task assignment stayed identical; detailed results are needed for that assessment.

blocks.title: Keep three distinctions in view
blocks.text: 100% quantity coverage does not establish on-time delivery. Two weights changed together, so this comparison cannot isolate either one's effect. Time and load fields must be interpreted in the dataset's units, not relabeled as minutes without conversion.

sections.title: Apply the approach to your own planning

items: Check that order, work-center, route, material and time identifiers connect correctly.
Separate mandatory conditions from soft constraints that can be expressed through a penalty.
Keep an approved baseline and, where possible, change one factor per comparison.
Review detailed plans and business measures with the planner responsible for accepting changes.

injection-molding.title: Injection molding: inspect the sequence after changing weights
injection-molding.intro: Color, product attributes and job order interact. A higher score or a larger weight only becomes meaningful when you examine the actual sequence and changeover counts.
injection-molding.context: Recorded 2026-08-31 · DecisioWorks v1.4.0 · Commercial Enterprise license · API records, not a live run on this page

blocks.text: How can changeover preferences be expressed when different products run consecutively? This example compares sequences after adjusting color- and container-capacity-related weights. It shows how to inspect trade-offs, rather than assuming that one adjustment will improve every measure.

sections.title: Input: how product attributes enter scheduling

blocks.caption: Main objects in this sample
rows: Changeover differences; container capacity is a product attribute

blocks.title: Distinguish stored data from new results
blocks.text: The input package already contained 120 result records; this run also returned 120 new rows. Use the run status and its outputs to establish completion, not simply the number of rows already in the database.

sections.title: Configuration: change preferences, retain comparison conditions

blocks.caption: Constraints and weights used in this comparison

blocks.text: The system reads attributes and compatibility relationships, builds constraints and objectives, and returns a sequence with analysis results. Keep both configurations and outputs. Compare physical changeover counts first, then examine weighted evaluation terms.

sections.title: Output: what did this re-run show?

blocks.caption: Baseline and re-run from the same API comparison

blocks.text: In this recorded comparison, changeover counts increased after the weights were raised. A feasible plan found within the available resources is not necessarily a proven global optimum. Scores calculated under different weights are also not an improvement percentage. Review sequences, business measures and constraint satisfaction together.

blocks.title: Use consistent evaluation definitions
blocks.text: Weighted cost includes model-specific evaluation terms and cannot be reconstructed by simply multiplying the displayed counts by the weights. Total API request time and the solver time limit measure different things. Because two attribute weights changed together, this comparison does not isolate either attribute's causal effect.

sections.title: What should the next comparison change?

items: Identify the changeover type you want to reduce and confirm attribute meanings and units.
Hold data and runtime resources constant; compare one preference change at a time.
Inspect adjacent jobs and cycle transitions to locate the changes.
Consider delivery, output and shop-floor conditions before keeping the result, adjusting again or returning to the baseline.

partners.title: Connect production decisions to your existing business
partners.intro: Begin with a clear data mapping, then bring plan generation, review and feedback into daily operations. Manufacturers retain business judgment, partners contribute domain and integration expertise, and DecisioWorks supplies shared decision capabilities.

blocks.text: Without ERP or MES, you can begin with spreadsheets and files. With those systems in place, completeness of business meaning and relationships remains the central question. Reuse the mapping and workflow in ongoing operation, then extend them to further scenarios.

Software partner, integrator or internal development team

blocks.text: DecisioCore can serve as an implementation reference: reuse code, extend domain logic or write your own code to call GOCK. Connecting the parts responsible for business, models and applications gives future changes a clear place to be handled.

sections.title: Where does value start to accumulate?

items: Data assets: shared definitions for orders, routes and resources, with reusable mappings and checks.
Decision evidence: turn verbal trade-off discussions into comparable configurations and results.
Industry assets: partners build their own rules, workflows, applications and examples on shared capabilities.
Ongoing operation: update the relevant data and rules as the business changes, retaining versions and feedback to improve planning over time.

blocks.text: Evaluate ROI against a consistently defined business baseline, such as planning effort, manual adjustments, delivery deviations and changeover losses. Include data preparation, integration and maintenance costs. Actual value depends on the scenario, data and execution conditions.

sections.title: Bring five things to an initial discussion

items: A recurring planning problem: the affected objects, time horizon and people.
An anonymized data sample: fields, units, identifiers and missing values.
A few key rules: what must be respected and what can be negotiated.
An existing plan and its deviations: how you judge a good result.
The people involved: who provides data, reviews results, integrates and operates the system.
